claims.name: Amazon Prime refunds (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: U.S. Prime members who signed up through a challenged enrollment flow or could not cancel online between June 23, 2019 and June 23, 2025, and used no more than 20 Prime benefits in any 12-month period after enrolling. Refunds are automatic; no claim, notice or form is needed.
claims.paymentTiming: Amazon began sending refunds in November 2025 and continues through April 2027; each payment expires 60 days after it is issued.

claims.name: Walmart money transfer refunds (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: people who completed eligible money transfers at Walmart between January 2015 and December 2024, in the FTC case over fraud-induced transfers. The FTC is mailing 65,022 checks totaling more than $9.8 million; payments are automatic.
claims.paymentTiming: Checks are being sent as of October 2026; cash your check within 90 days.

claims.name: Cleo AI cash advance refunds (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: people who paid Cleo AI for cash advances that were smaller or slower than promised, or who had trouble cancelling. The FTC is sending 2,124,796 PayPal payments totaling more than $15.8 million; eligible people get an email first and no claim is needed.
claims.paymentTiming: Notification emails October 8-26, 2026; PayPal payments start October 27, 2026 and must be accepted within 30 days.

claims.name: AdvoCare second refunds (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: former AdvoCare distributors who accepted their first FTC payment (sent May 2022) in the pyramid scheme case. A second round of 170,571 payments totaling more than $11.4 million is automatic.
claims.paymentTiming: Second payments are being sent as of October 2026; cash checks within 90 days, accept PayPal within 30 days.

claims.name: Avast second refunds (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: Avast antivirus customers who filed a valid claim by June 5, 2025 and accepted their first payment (sent December 2025), in the FTC case over selling users' browsing data. A second round of 91,093 payments totaling more than $1.5 million is automatic; no new claims are accepted.
claims.paymentTiming: Second payments are being sent as of October 2026; cash checks within 90 days. PayPal and Zelle payments are deposited directly.

claims.name: GOAT expedited shipping refunds (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: GOAT marketplace customers who paid for expedited shipping between 2020 and 2024, got their order late, and did not get a refund from GOAT. The FTC is sending 6,205 payments totaling more than $100,000; payments are automatic.
claims.paymentTiming: Payments are being sent as of October 2026; cash checks within 90 days, accept PayPal within 30 days.

claims.name: AT&T data throttling refunds (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: former AT&T unlimited-data customers whose speeds were throttled and who did not cash the FTC check or accept the PayPal payment sent earlier. The FTC is now sending the money by Zelle, deposited directly into the bank account; no claim is needed.
claims.paymentTiming: Zelle payments are being sent as of August 2026; the first checks went out in April 2024.

claims.name: Grubhub driver and diner refunds (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: Grubhub drivers harmed by deceptive claims about earnings, and diners harmed by misleading and unlawful conduct such as blocked accounts with unused gift card balances. The FTC is sending 640,038 payments totaling more than $23.8 million; payments are automatic.
claims.paymentTiming: Payments are being sent as of August 2026; cash checks within 90 days, accept PayPal within 30 days.

claims.name: Helping America Group debt relief refunds (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: people who paid Helping America Group for debt relief it never delivered and who accepted the second FTC payment. A third round of 9,522 payments totaling more than $463,000 is automatic (FTC and Florida Attorney General case).
claims.paymentTiming: Third-round checks are being sent as of August 2026; cash within 90 days. Earlier rounds went out July 2020 and December 2021.

claims.name: Blueprint to Wealth refunds (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: people who paid for the Blueprint to Wealth business opportunity, which falsely promised big earnings, and who accepted their first FTC payment (sent September 2025). A second round of 2,005 payments totaling more than $333,000 is automatic.
claims.paymentTiming: Second payments are being sent as of August 2026; cash checks within 90 days, accept PayPal within 30 days.

claims.name: Fortnite refunds (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: Fortnite players charged for unwanted in-game items between January 2017 and September 2022, parents whose child made charges without their knowledge between January 2017 and November 2018, or players locked out after disputing charges. Claims closed July 9, 2025; the FTC says it expects to send additional payments in 2026 after reviewing the remaining claims.
claims.paymentTiming: First round of 969,173 payments (more than $126 million) sent June 2025; additional payments expected in 2026.

claims.name: NGL app refunds (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: people who paid for NGL Pro between January 2022 and July 2024, had unauthorized charges, and filed a claim by April 6, 2026. Claims are closed; the FTC expects to send payments in 2026 after reviewing all claims.
claims.paymentTiming: Payments expected in 2026 after claim review; the settlement fund is $4.5 million.

claims.name: Golden Sunrise refunds (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: people who bought Golden Sunrise treatment plans sold between July 2017 and July 2020 as cures for COVID-19, cancer and other diseases, and who filed a valid claim by May 12, 2026. Claims are closed; first checks went out in February 2026 and more payments are expected in late 2026.
claims.paymentTiming: 578 checks totaling more than $40,700 sent February 2026; additional payments expected in late 2026.

claims.name: First American Payment Systems refunds (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: small businesses that enrolled with First American Payment Systems between June 2017 and April 2020 and were charged an early termination fee. Eligible businesses got letters with a Claim ID; to apply, call the claims administrator at 1-877-595-0114. The FTC is still reviewing claims.
claims.paymentTiming: 5,588 checks totaling more than $2.6 million were sent in February 2025; claim review is ongoing.

claims.name: Vivint credit report misuse payments (FTC)
claims.summary: Who gets money: people who never signed up for Vivint's home security service but had a Vivint account opened in their name between 2016 and 2019 because their credit report was misused. The FTC says you can still apply by calling the administrator at 1-833-472-1996.
claims.paymentTiming: 470 checks totaling nearly $500,000 went to earlier claimants in December 2024; later applicants are paid after review.

claims.name: Navient student loan payments (CFPB)
claims.summary: Who gets money: borrowers the CFPB identified as steered into forbearance instead of income-driven repayment, and people whose discharged student loans were misreported by Pioneer Credit Recovery. Checks are automatic and claims are not accepted; a payment does not change your loan balance.
claims.paymentTiming: Checks have been going out since February 13, 2026; the CFPB listed the distribution as ongoing on October 26, 2026.

claims.name: Lexington Law and CreditRepair.com payments (CFPB)
claims.summary: Who gets money: customers the CFPB identified as harmed by Lexington Law and CreditRepair.com's illegal advance fees. A second payment goes automatically to people who cashed their first check by June 30, 2026 and are owed $10 or more. If you never got your first check, request a reissue through the administrator's contact form or call 1-855-680-8991.
claims.paymentTiming: Second payments (about $117 million) mailed from late September through October 2026; checks are valid for 90 days.

claims.name: Hello Digit savings app payments (CFPB)
claims.summary: Who gets money: consumers the CFPB identified as harmed by Digit's automated savings app, which the CFPB says caused overdrafts and did not reimburse the fees as promised. Payments come from the CFPB Civil Penalty Fund through administrator Epiq (1-888-860-1014); no claim is needed.
claims.paymentTiming: Email notifications went out October 15, 2026; the CFPB lists the distribution as ongoing.

claims.name: Climb Credit loan refunds (CFPB)
claims.summary: Who gets money: borrowers whose Climb Credit loan disclosures left origination fees out of the finance charge. Refunds from the CFPB Civil Penalty Fund are automatic; questions go to Rust Consulting at 1-800-889-6288.
claims.paymentTiming: Distribution began July 24, 2026 and is listed as ongoing.

claims.name: Easy Military Travel refunds (CFPB)
claims.summary: Who gets money: consumers affected by Easy Military Travel's airline ticket loans, which the CFPB says hid the true finance charge and total cost. Refunds from the Civil Penalty Fund are automatic; questions go to Rust Consulting at 1-877-788-4957.
claims.paymentTiming: Distribution began July 9, 2026 and is listed as ongoing.

claims.name: Performant Recovery student loan payments (CFPB)
claims.summary: Who gets money: borrowers with defaulted FFEL student loans whose help was delayed by debt collector Performant Recovery. Checks were mailed to identified consumers; cash them right away, no information needed.
claims.paymentTiming: Checks mailed from May 29, 2026; the CFPB lists the distribution as ongoing.

claims.name: Fay Servicing mortgage redress (CFPB)
claims.summary: Who gets money: mortgage borrowers covered by the CFPB's order against Fay Servicing for violating a 2017 order; the company paid $3 million in consumer redress. Payments are automatic; questions go to Rust Consulting at 1-800-804-3454.
claims.paymentTiming: Distribution began March 6, 2026 and is listed as ongoing.

claims.name: Mortgage Law Group fee refunds (CFPB)
claims.defendant: The Mortgage Law Group and Consumer First Legal Group
claims.summary: Who gets money: people who paid fees to The Mortgage Law Group or Consumer First Legal Group for mortgage relief; the CFPB says they charged illegal up-front fees and made false statements. Refunds are automatic; questions go to Rust Consulting at 1-800-890-9169.
claims.paymentTiming: Distribution began March 10, 2026 and is listed as ongoing.

claims.name: Reverse mortgage servicing refunds (CFPB)
claims.summary: Who gets money: reverse mortgage (home equity conversion mortgage) borrowers whose loans were serviced by the Sutherland companies, which the CFPB says sent incorrect repayment letters and ignored requests, leaving borrowers fearing foreclosure or paying needless costs. Refunds are automatic; questions go to Rust Consulting at 1-800-731-9353.
claims.paymentTiming: Distribution began January 30, 2026 and is listed as ongoing.

claims.name: Western Benefits Group payments (CFPB)
claims.summary: Who gets money: consumers who signed up with Western Benefits Group for student loan debt relief; the CFPB found it broke the Telemarketing Sales Rule and voided its agreements. Civil Penalty Fund payments are automatic; questions go to Rust Consulting at 1-800-419-5275.
claims.paymentTiming: Distribution began January 28, 2026 and is listed as ongoing.

claims.name: Veterans pension advance payments (CFPB)
claims.defendant: Mark Corbett, Andrew Gamber and related defendants
claims.summary: Who gets money: veterans and others who were told they could sell their pension or disability payments when the deals were really high-cost loans that the CFPB says were void (Corbett, Gamber, Kern-Fuller and Snyder cases). Checks are mailed to identified consumers, and people who believe they qualify can submit a claim at corbettgamberpayment.org or call Rust Consulting at 1-877-552-1282.
claims.paymentTiming: Distribution began December 27, 2023; the CFPB lists it as ongoing.

claims.name: Generic drug price-fixing claims (state AGs)
claims.defendant: Apotex, Heritage, Bausch, Lannett and Glenmark
claims.summary: Who gets money: consumers who overpaid for certain generic prescription drugs (for example digoxin) because of price fixing; settlements with Apotex, Heritage, Bausch, Lannett and Glenmark reached by a coalition of state attorneys general total more than $96 million. File a claim at AGGenericDrugs.com, by email to info@aggenericdrugs.com, or by calling 1-866-290-0182 by March 8, 2027.
claims.paymentTiming: Payments after the claim deadline, claim review and court approval of the distribution plan (U.S. District Court, District of Connecticut).

claims.name: FC&A free-preview book refunds (NY AG)
claims.summary: Who gets money: people who paid for a self-help book that FC&A mailed to a New York address on a 'free no-risk preview' basis within the last six years. Refunds are in full; contact FC&A directly before April 23, 2027.
